interpretation_limits: The overall composite hazard ratio is not a mortality-only effect.
The mortality hazard ratio is not an absolute risk reduction.
This comparison does not establish superiority over tafamidis; monotherapy participants were not on tafamidis at baseline.
Similar reported adverse-event frequency does not establish absence of safety risk.

claim_audit.claim: HELIOS-B enrolled/randomized 655 participants in a Phase 3 placebo-controlled trial.
Published overall composite HR is 0.72 (95% CI 0.56-0.93); mortality through 42 months is a separate endpoint, HR 0.65 (0.46-0.90).
The US ATTR-CM indication was approved March 20, 2025.
The realized US approval decision removes uncertainty over whether that historical decision occurred, while leaving launch economics uncertain.
The illustrative predecision approval gate is 0.60; no trial hazard ratio or p-value calibrates this probability.

existing_case_reconciliation: C03's broader Q2-2026 commercial scope is not verified here. The retrieved NEJM abstract reports mortality HR 0.65, equivalent to a 35% relative hazard reduction for that analysis. Any 36% claim requires its own document, time point and analysis population; do not silently substitute one estimate for the other.
